speaker_concepts.verbatim_description: The EMA10 tracks short-term momentum. It's fast. It reacts immediately to price changes.
The EMA 20 is smoother. It represents the broader short to medium-term trend.
The commodity channel index was designed to measure how far the current price has moved away from its average price over a certain period.
CCI often crosses above zero before the EMA crossover happens. Read that again. Before, this is your early warning system.
When the EMA10 crosses above the EMA20, it signals that recent momentum is accelerating upward. That's bullish.
When the EMA10 crosses below the EMA20, momentum is shifting down. That's bearish.
CCI must be above zero at the time of the crossover or it must have crossed above zero shortly before. This confirms the momentum has strength.
